title: The Reinebold Report
subtitle: "Football is a game of leverage, angles, and finding the man who forgot to start his running back."
tagline: Week 2 — The Recap Nobody Asked For
author: Jeff Reinebold
lede: Well folks, welcome back to the film room. Week 2 is where the frauds get exposed and the studs get paid — and boy, did we get paid. Jaxon Smith-Njigba put up a number that looks like a phone bill, a defense turned in a 20-spot, and one poor soul scored 82 and got sent home to think about it. Two teams sit undefeated and one 'Dream Team' is 0-2 and living a nightmare. Pour the coffee. Reinebold's got the tape.

matchups.recap: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (42.5) went absolutely nuclear — a league-high that carried the day almost by himself — with Dalton Kincaid (22.5) and a tidy 16 from kicker Harrison Butker doing the rest. AllInTheTush got a big TE line from Travis Kelce (25.1) and steady work from Omarion Hampton (17.5), but Zay Flowers sat on the bench with a 0.0, Jameson Williams (5.3) whiffed, and Malik Nabers (1.1) was invisible.
matchups.trashTalk: AllInTheTush brought a Tush Push and Questionable or Kicked brought a rocket ship. JSN alone outscored four of that lineup combined. Maybe it's 'AllInTheLoss' this week.

matchups.recap: The heavyweight bout of the week and a league-best 154.42. Davante Adams (39.5) and Ja'Marr Chase (26.5) went off, the Patriots D/ST posted a monster 20.0, and Trey McBride (18.1) chipped in. Mauled by the Panthers put up a respectable 131.6 behind Amon-Ra St. Brown (35.2) and balanced backfield work, but Lamar Jackson (14.8) was quiet and it just wasn't enough against a buzzsaw.
matchups.trashTalk: Mauled by the Panthers scored 131 and STILL got mauled. Davante Adams alone nearly tripled that quarterback. The Lambs aren't so silent now, are they?

matchups.recap: Josh Allen (40.82) did his best Superman impression and DeVonta Smith (27.7) rode shotgun as Champ finally backed up the name. Kelce's Wildest Dream Team actually got the QB call right — Mahomes (28.98) over the benched Stafford in a one-QB league — and Jahmyr Gibbs (23.3) and Chris Olave (22.6) held up their end. The problem was everywhere else: Colston Loveland (1.3), Dallas Goedert (1.4) out of the FLEX, and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (5.8) gave them almost nothing.
matchups.trashTalk: Kelce's Wildest Dream Team got the big fellas going and still lost — because the tight ends combined for less than three and the flex forgot to show. Two studs, a bunch of no-shows, and an 0-2 hole. That's the nightmare, not the dream.

matchups.recap: Redemption for the mascot! CeeDee Lamb (35.3) went bananas, James Cook III (20.9) ran hard, and even the Buccaneers D/ST behaved this time. Cracked Out Uncle got a bell-cow game from Jonathan Taylor (29.2) and Sam LaPorta (17.2), but Cameron Dicker's 1.0 and Travis Etienne (7.1) left the tank empty in a game it lost by 11.38.
matchups.trashTalk: Cracked Out Uncle is back at 0-2 — but hey, this week the good players actually made the lineup. Small victories. That kicker scored a single point, though; even Major Tuddy's mascot outscored that.

matchups.recap: Bang average lived up to nothing but the W here, riding Bryce Young (24.08), Kenneth Walker III (23.8), and a bounce-back 21.8 from Jaylen Waddle. False Hope earned its name — a week-low 82.36 as Saquon Barkley (3.0), David Montgomery (4.4), and Trevor Lawrence (6.16) all no-showed, DJ Moore actually went NEGATIVE at -0.1, and Blake Corum's 10.2 rotted on the bench.
matchups.trashTalk: False Hope? That's just accurate branding. Scored 82 with Saquon and CMC on the roster, a starting receiver went NEGATIVE, and the best bench points stayed benched. That's not hope, that's a cry for help.

awards.label: Stud of the Week
awards.note: A one-man wrecking crew. Nearly won the matchup solo.

awards.label: Workhorse Award
awards.note: Ran downhill all day — wasted in a loss.

awards.label: Bust of the Week
awards.note: A starting WR that scored LESS than zero.

awards.label: Bench Blunder
awards.note: Benched Corum (10.2) while Montgomery (4.4) started. Lost by 48.

awards.label: Defensive Disaster
awards.note: A dollar-store defense in a shootout week.

awards.label: Surprise of the Week
awards.note: Turned back the clock and torched the Panthers.

momentOfWeek.text: False Hope scoring a week-low 82.36 in a 48-point loss — with Saquon Barkley and Christian McCaffrey on the roster, a starting receiver in DJ Moore going NEGATIVE, and Blake Corum's 10.2 left stapled to the bench. When the studs sleep AND the lineup's wrong, that's how you land in the film room for all the wrong reasons. Set. Your. Lineup.
momentOfWeek.attribution: — from the film room, Coach Reinebold

powerRankings.take: Undefeated and JSN just erased a whole roster.
League-best score, 2-0, and mean about it.
Josh Allen went nuclear. Finally a real Champ.
Scored 131 and lost. Brutal week to draw the Lambs.
Waddle bounced back. Right on brand — solid, not scary.
CeeDee carried the barn. Mascot back in the win column.
Kelce and Hampton showed; the rest RSVP'd no.
Week-low 82 with a negative WR. Nominative determinism.
Set the lineup right and STILL 0-2. Rough start.
Two studs carried; the tight ends sank it. 0-2.

lastWord: That's Week 2, gang. We learned JSN can win a game by himself, a receiver can score negative points, and two studs won't save you when the tight ends no-show. Two teams are undefeated, two are winless, and the fastest way to join the losers is to leave points on your bench. Set your lineups, trust your studs, and False Hope — start somebody, anybody. Reinebold out.
